body:
## Problem

POSIX-compatible Ex-mode requires special-cases all over the codebase to match various little quirks that don't actually matter to users.

- The main utility of *interactive* Ex-mode is its REPL behavior, and that can be achieved with `cmdwin`, which also gains extra UX benefits.
- The main utility of *non-interactive* `nvim -es` is for shell scripting, where the old Ex-mode quirks are actually not that useful (e.g. "Entering Ex mode" message is _unwanted_ for scripts).

## Solution

- Reimplement *interactive* Ex-mode as a "persistent, insert-mode cmdwin" in Lua.
    - `nvim -e/-E` is simply an alias to `gQ`.
- Reframe *non-interactive* Ex-mode (`nvim -es`) as "script mode".
    - Drop POSIX Ex-mode quirks.

See commit msg for details.

Fix https://github.com/neovim/neovim/issues/40962
Fix https://github.com/neovim/neovim/issues/40966

comment_data.body:
TODO(?): could enhance `nvim_exec2` instead, with new `opts`:

- `getline: fun():string?` : line-getter used instead of `src` (`nil` = EOF). `do_cmdline()` pulls lines on demand, so `:append`/`:function`/heredoc/`:if` consume continuation lines lazily from stdin.
- `once: boolean` : execute exactly one logical command, so the caller can pump events between commands. Adds `got_line: boolean` to the result (`false` = EOF, ends the loop).
- `throw: boolean` (default `true`) : `false` = script semantics: errors are emitted (stderr with `-V1`) instead of thrown, execution continues with the next command, `ex_exitval` still sets the exit code, output streams instead of being captured.

`exmode.run()` becomes:

    while nvim_exec2('', {getline=..., once=true, throw=false}).got_line do vim.wait(0) end

`block_complete()` uses the same mechanism wrapped in `if v:false … endif`.

Open questions:
- whether `once` requires `getline`
- whether `throw=false` implies streaming (`output=false`)

comment_regular_data.body: Besides the code simplification, this is mildly helpful for mmmmmmulticursor because it reveals that `gQ` doesn't really need to be a builtin Ex-mode entrypoint. Which means `gQ` can be used for multicursor instead.

Line continuation work as expected but are missing visual feedback.
For example, on master, `gQfunction Foo()` gives an automatic line indent to indicate an open block, and
`gQinsert<cr>` removes the leading `:` which makes sense as what is typed next is not a command.

Not saying it needs to look exactly the same, but _some_ indication of a continuation line would be nice.
> Line continuation work as expected but are missing visual feedback. Now it looks like this: I did not add "indent" because that complicates the code.
